answers.evidence: पर मास्टर जी ने सबके हाथ पकड़वा दिए।
answers.note: Every Indian school kid has stood in a ground circle on a hot noon holding a neighbour's hand.

answers.evidence: किसी ने मेरा हाथ पकड़ा। चालीस डिग्री में भी, हाथ ठंडा था।
answers.note: The narrator is forced into the violation by the teacher, so it is not his choice.

answers.evidence: मैंने हाथ छुड़ाया। मेरी परछाईं राजू के पैरों से जुड़ी रही।
answers.note: Physical and visible: a shadow stays attached to the wrong feet.

answers.evidence: वो राजू था। बाल गीले, बूँद टपकती हुई।
answers.note: Shadows go, cold hand, then the face and the drop. Each step removes a safety.

answers.evidence: फिर एक एक करके, सबकी परछाईं गायब हो गई।
answers.note: Raju's face is shown only in the 6 s before the whisper and half in frame. Nothing explains how the swap works beyond Dadi's one rule.
Details in no other script: a noon with no shadows, a wet hand in 40 degree heat, a drop evaporating on hot stone, one shadow for two boys.

answers.evidence: मेरी परछाईं राजू के पैरों से जुड़ी रही।
answers.note: Recontextualises the hook: the school's shadows were gone because the dead one came for the one that returns.

answers.evidence: उसने धीरे से कहा, एक ही परछाईं लौटती है।
answers.note: Cicadas die as the shadows go, then 1 s of silence before the whisper stinger.

answers.evidence: परछाईं गायब हो, तो किसी का हाथ मत पकड़ना।
answers.note: Short and final. The last shot returns to the foot-level wet footprints of the opening.
The narrator-is-the-ghost idea is a known trope, and 'only one comes back' is a known swap rule. Fresh part is the mechanism and the daylight setting.
